import numpy as np
from pandas.core.dtypes.missing import array_equivalent

# Example 1: complex(1, np.nan) vs complex(2, np.nan) - differ in real part, both have NaN imaginary
result1 = array_equivalent(
    np.array([complex(1, np.nan)], dtype='c16'),
    np.array([complex(2, np.nan)], dtype='c16'),
    dtype_equal=True
)
probe('example1_real_part_differs_imag_nan', float(result1))

# Example 2: complex(np.nan, 1) vs complex(np.nan, 2) - both have NaN real, differ in imaginary
result2 = array_equivalent(
    np.array([complex(np.nan, 1)], dtype='c16'),
    np.array([complex(np.nan, 2)], dtype='c16'),
    dtype_equal=True
)
probe('example2_real_nan_imag_differs', float(result2))

# Example 3: mixed array with one valid and one NaN element
result3 = array_equivalent(
    np.array([1+2j, complex(3, np.nan)], dtype='c16'),
    np.array([1+2j, complex(9, np.nan)], dtype='c16'),
    dtype_equal=True
)
probe('example3_mixed_valid_and_nan', float(result3))

# Example 4: both elements differ in valid part, second has NaN
result4 = array_equivalent(
    np.array([1+2j, complex(3, np.nan)], dtype='c16'),
    np.array([5+2j, complex(9, np.nan)], dtype='c16'),
    dtype_equal=True
)
probe('example4_valid_parts_differ_with_nan', float(result4))
